title: Qualitative systematic review of burnout in sub-Saharan African healthcare workers
author: Imre Papp

steps.title: Perform Database Search
steps.instruction: Search MEDLINE, Global Health Database, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and CINAHL using search terms related to burnout concepts, health worker populations, and sub-Saharan African geographic locations.

substeps.instruction: Use burnout concepts: burnout, compassion fatigue, occupational stress, desire to leave, attrition, job satisfaction
Use health worker populations: healthcare workers, nurses, community health workers, physicians, midwives
Use geographic locations: sub-Saharan African countries or capital cities
If satisfied with results, save the search string, record the date, and download the RIS file
If not satisfied, refine the search and reassess before recording the search string

steps.title: Manage Search Results
steps.instruction: Upload the downloaded RIS files to Covidence software for review and remove duplicate entries.

substeps.instruction: Allow Covidence to automatically remove most duplicates
Manually remove any remaining duplicates

steps.title: Screen for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Screen studies based on title relevance and full-text review according to specific inclusion and exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Apply inclusion criteria: English language, qualitative or mixed methodology, set in sub-Saharan Africa, focus on healthcare workers (community health workers, physicians, midwives, clinical officers, nurses, and others directly engaging in patient care), examine burnout or job satisfaction, and peer-reviewed publications

Apply exclusion criteria: non-English language, exclusively quantitative methodology, not set in sub-Saharan Africa, articles focusing on burnout due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and studies focusing on mental health workers
Perform title relevance screening with two independent reviewers
Conduct a full-text review of remaining studies to determine final eligibility
Resolve any disagreements between reviewers through discussion to reach a consensus

steps.title: Extract Descriptive Data
steps.instruction: Extract descriptive data from each included study into a spreadsheet with the following 15 fields: 1) title, 2) author, 3) year of publication, 4) country and setting of study, 5) aim of study, 6) study design, 7) start/end date, 8) population, 9) inclusion criteria, 10) # of participants, 11) identified themes/subthemes, 12) important quotes, 13) synthesis of results, 14) limitations, 15) notes.

steps.title: Assess Methodological Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the methodological quality of included studies and the confidence in findings.

substeps.instruction: Use the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) Qualitative Checklist to assess study design, data collection, reflexivity, ethical considerations, and rigor of analysis
Conduct quality appraisal independently with at least two reviewers and resolve disagreements via discussion
Assess confidence in review findings using the GRADE-CERQual approach
Evaluate each finding across four domains: Methodological limitations, Coherence, Adequacy of data, and Relevance
Assign an overall confidence level (high, moderate, low, or very low) to each finding and produce a summary of qualitative findings table

steps.title: Perform Thematic Synthesis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using Thomas and Harden's thematic synthesis approach, utilizing qualitative data analysis software (e.g., Quirkos).

substeps.instruction: Conduct iterative line-by-line coding on findings sections to generate inductive codes
Have a subset of studies independently coded by at least two reviewers and resolve discrepancies by consensus
Group codes into descriptive themes using a constant comparative approach to examine similarities and differences
Develop analytical themes through interpretive analysis and research team discussion to generate higher-order insights
Support key themes with illustrative participant quotes and maintain an audit trail of analytical decisions

description: Limitations: English-language, published between January 1, 2000, and December 2, 2025. Repeat step 7, this time assessing abstract relevance to determine potential eligibility.
